history.summary: The Dakhina Kali Temple of the CSV is the Maa Dakhinakali Temple in Nayagarh town (Mishra Colony/Old Town, on National Highway 224, Nayagarh-752070), Nayagarh district, Odisha. It is dedicated to Goddess Dakshina Kali - described in one write-up as a benign and kind form of Mother Kali who fulfils the wishes of devotees. The temple follows typical Odisha-style architecture and the complex also houses shrines of Shiva, Ganesha and Lakshmi. One travel vlogger calls it a living Shakti-peeth of Nayagarh (verify). The most important festival is Pana Sankranti (April 14/15); Chaturdashi and Amavasya observances and Kali Puja are also major. CSV town 'Nayagarh' is correct in the broad sense - the temple is in Nayagarh town itself, on NH-224 at Mishra Colony/Old Town (one listing also tags it 'Dimisar' - verify the precise locality). It is distinct from the famous Ladubaba (Sarankul), Nilamadhab (Kantilo) and Raghunathjew (Odagaon) temples of the same district.

town_description: Nayagarh is a town and the district headquarters of Nayagarh district, Odisha, about 90 km from Bhubaneswar. It is known for its temples - the Dakshinakali shrine in town, plus the famous Ladubaba (Sarankul), Nilamadhab (Kantilo) and Raghunathjew (Odagaon) temples nearby - and for the Kuanria Dam and Similipal-adjacent forest belt.
